AGENDA

  5:00 PM Closed Session
  6:00 PM Regular Meeting

  Council Chambers
  MAYOR AND CITY COUNCIL  2000 Main Street  STAFF
  BARBARA DELGLEIZE, Mayor  Huntington Beach, CA 92648  SEAN JOYCE, Interim City Manager
  MIKE POSEY, Mayor Pro Tem  MICHAEL E. GATES, City Attorney
  --or--
  RHONDA BOLTON, Councilmember  ROBIN ESTANISLAU, City Clerk
  KIM CARR, Councilmember  Virtual via Zoom Webinar  ALISA BACKSTROM, City Treasurer
  DAN KALMICK, Councilmember
  NATALIE MOSER, Councilmember
  ERIK PETERSON, Councilmember

IN-PERSON PUBLIC PARTICIPATION/ZOOM ACCESS:  Members  wishing  to  attend  the  meeting
in person are encouraged to wear a face covering.
Assembly Bill 361 (AB 361) authorizes public meetings to take place via teleconference (i.e., virtual
using Zoom), or in person if in part, State and Local officials continue to recommend measures to
promote social distancing.  In addition to this hybrid format, alternate ways to view City Council
meetings live or on-demand remain:  livestreamed on HBTV Channel 3 (replayed on Wednesday’s at
10:00 a.m. and Thursday’s at 6:00 p.m.); live and archived meetings for on-demand viewing accessed
from https://huntingtonbeach.legistar.com/calendar; or, from any Roku, Fire TV or Apple device by
downloading the Cablecast Screenweave App and searching for the City of Huntington Beach channel.
PUBLIC COMMENTS:  Individuals wishing to provide a comment on agendized or non -agendized
items, including Study Session, Closed Session, and Public Hearing, may do so in person by
completing a Request to Speak form delivered to the City Clerk, or from a virtual location by entering
Zoom Webinar ID 971 5413 0528 via computer device, or by phone at (669) 900-6833.  The Zoom
Webinar can be accessed here: https://huntingtonbeach.zoom.us/j/97154130528.  Instructions for
those utilizing computer devices to request to speak are provided in each section of the agenda where
public comments are accepted.
Members of the public unable to personally participate in the meeting but interested in communicating
with the City Council on agenda-related items are encouraged to submit a written (supplemental)
communication via email at  SupplementalComm@Surfcity-hb.org, or City.Council@surfcity-hb.org.
Supplemental Communications are public record, and if received by 2:00 PM on the day of the meeting,
will be distributed to the City Council prior to consideration of agenda -related items, posted to the City
website, and announced, but not read, at the meeting. Communications received following the 2:00 PM
deadline will be incorporated into the administrative record.
MEETING ASSISTANCE NOTICE: In accordance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, services
are available to members of our community who require special assistance to participate in public
meetings. If you require special assistance, 48-hour prior notification will enable the City to make
reasonable arrangements for an assisted listening device (ALD) for the hearing impaired, American
Sign Language interpreters, a reader during the meeting and /or large print agendas. Please contact the
City Clerk's Office at (714) 536-5227 for more information.

23.. Consider placing Charter amendments on ballot measures for voter approval during the November 2022 General Elections; recognize the completion of the Charter Revision Committee’s scope of work and dissolve the Committee accordingly  -  Action: approved (Pass) Moved by Dan Kalmick {\rtf1\ansi\ansicpg1252\deff0\deflang1033{\fonttbl{\f0\fnil\fcharset0 Arial;}}
{\colortbl ;\red0\green0\blue0;}
\viewkind4\uc1\pard\cf1\fs24 Catherine Jun, Assistant to the City Manager presented a PP presentation with slides entitled: Recommend Charter Amendments for Voter Approval at November Elections; Background; Today; Outcome; Proposed Ballot Measure 1; Proposed Ballot Measure 1 (continued); Proposed Ballot Measure 2; Remaining Amendments Proposed by the Committee; Suggested Amendments from City Representatives; Suggested Amendments from City Representatives (Continued); Recommended Actions.\par
\par
Councilmember Carr clarified the procedure for discussion on this item. She questioned how many times they would have to bring this back for discussion/changes prior to submitting for the election. City Attorney Gates confirmed that as long as the language was decided it would not have to come back.\par
Kalmick believes "bucket 1" is reasonable. He expressed that procedure for filling the vacancy is a priority for him and would solve potential future issues. \par
Councilmember Carr agreed with Kalmick and wants to add some of the suggestions such as 311(d) to bucket 1.\par
Councilmember Moser concurred with discussion thus far. \par
Mayor Pro Tem Posey expressed that he liked the appointment process to fill the vacancy as well as the charter review requirement. \par
Councilmember Carr added that she agreed with ballot measure c on listed "bucket 1" pertaining to parks and open space.\par
Mayor Pro Tem Posey acknowledged the speakers that had shared concerns regarding not making changes pertaining to certain items within the charter.\par
  \par
\par
Councilmember Moser shared her support for regular review to the "living document" that is the City Charter. \par
Councilmember Bolton shared that this is a foundation document. or a living document similar to the US Constitution (which as been revised numerous times). She is not opposed to anything on ballot measure 1.\par
\par
Councilmember Posey clarified that the 10 year review is the maximum. Any Council can come in and decide to review it prior. \par
\par
\par
Councilmember Kalmick expressed why Mayor Pro Tem should be changed to Vice Mayor as it is easier to understand what the position is. \par
Mayor Delgleize supports that change as does Mayor Pro Tem Posey.\par
\par
Discussion on "bucket 2" \par
Councilmember Kalmick shared that he would amend 309 - to remove the ABA requirement. He supports the term "practicing" vs. "licensed". \par
Councilmember Carr would leave the current charter pertaining to the City Attorney position it as is right now (5 years practicing) with the removal of the ABA requirement. \par
Councilmember Bolton concurred with Councilmember Carr's comments. \par
\par
Discussion "bucket 3" \par
Councilmember Kalmick provided context pertaining the Clerk & Treasurer positions as having been appointed upon a vacancy and then having been elected. He expressed his opinion that the City Attorney, Clerk & Treasurer positions all follow policies set by the City Council, therefor they are in working for the City Council. Identifying the Clerk and Treasurer as "Department Heads". \par
Councilmember Carr recognized the amazing efforts of City Clerk Robin Estanislau and commended her for her hard work and dedication. She praised the City Treasurer Alyssa Cutchen as well and expressed concern about the future talent pool with these positions. \par
Councilmember Bolton agreed with Councilmember Carr, that these positions are highly specialized that they should use the same recruiting process as they would for CM, Police & Fire Chief positions. \par
Mayor Delgleize agreed with previous comments.  \par
\par
\par
Councilmember Moser agreed that City Clerk being a technical position should be recruited to widen the pool of applicants.\par
\par
Straw Vote: Item #1\par
Kalmick - motion to move City Clerk & City Treasurer as appointed as a separate item on the ballot.\par
Delgleize 2nd \par
6-0-1 (Peterson absent) \par
\par
Item #2 (Convert City Attorney from an elected to appointed role)\par
Mayor Pro Tem Posey - spoke regarding how the authority is with the majority of CC regardless if the CA is elected or appointed. The authority to sue or not rests with the CC. \par
Mayor Delgleize shared that the language in the Charter is not clear, or grammatically correct and ambiguous. Spoke that asking for a 2nd opinion doesn't remove the authority of the CA. \par
Councilmember Carr shared her concern that the City be able to attract the top talent for the position. There are only 10 cities in CA that have elected City Attorney's. Doesn't believe the the position should be politicized. She expressed that the wording needs to be clarified. Suggested to keep the position elected but the clarify the language of the position. \par
Councilmember Bolton commented regarding the attorney/client relationship and how the situation that we are currently facing is due to the lack of clarity in the wording of the charter. Expressed that we shouldn't be in this situation specifically due to the ethics rules.  \par
\par
Councilmember Moser reinforced that the CA role/job is to enforce the municipal code and advise the CC.\par
\par
Straw Vote #5 (Amendments from City Representatives) - 304(b), 309, & Create Section 310 (take a 2nd look at (b) for language clarification) \par
Motion - Carr\par
2nd - Bolton\par
6-0-1\par
\par
Straw Vote to Add cancellation of CC meetings to "bucket 1 verbiage" add 303(a) to Measure 1\par
Motion - Kalmick\par
2nd Mayor Delgleize\par
6-0-1\par
\par
Mayor Pro Tem Posey suggested increasing the CC term limits to be 3 - 4 year terms, for a total of 12 years on CC. \par
Councilmember Kalmick clarified the timing of the limits, when do they start? Would they be retroactive? \par
City Attorney Gates advised they could write it however the Council wants.\par
Councilmember Carr is not in favor of extending the term limits and doesn't believe the voters would be either.\par
\par
\par
Motion to continue the meeting past 11pm by Kalmick 2nd by Mayor Delgleize\par
\par
City Clerk Robin Estanislau summarized:\par
Ballot Measure 1 - items 1 thru 11 include 306,  311(d) and add 303(a) - "Bucket 1"\par
Ballot Measure 2 - item 2 - sections 310 & 311 with removal of ABA requirement \par
Ballot Measure 3 - item 1 with City Clerk & Treasurer appointed not elected\par
Ballot Measure 4 - item 5 sections 304(b), 309 & 310 with 310(2b) being reviewed.\par
